ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle, with the center point labeled X. There are two straight lines passing through X: one is Z-X-W, and the other is Y-X-V. The angle in the upper part inside the circle formed by rays XZ and XV is labeled (2x+65)°, and the vertical angle below formed by rays XY and XW is labeled (4x+15)°. What is asked for is ∠ZXY, that is, the angle between rays XZ and XY. Reasoning: Because (2x+65)° and (4x+15)° are vertical angles formed by the intersection of two straight lines, they are equal: 2x+65=4x+15. Solving gives 50=2x, so x=25. Thus the labeled angle is 2x+65=2(25)+65=115°. ∠ZXY is adjacent to this 115° angle, and they form a linear pair on a straight line, so they are supplementary. Therefore m∠ZXY=180°-115°=65°.

The requested angle ∠ZXY is adjacent to it along the straight line Y-X-V, so it is supplementary: m∠ZXY = 180 - 115 = 65.
